items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I recorded ... with Edgar Courance (tenor), John Ferrier (piano), Oscar Aleman (guitar), Eugene d'Hellemes (bass), and William Diemar (drums).

ctx.x: D'Hellemes was a good solid bass player who preferred to play trombone. He was also a very agreable fellow and we began to be good friends although I did not speak French and he didn't speak English. The first date with Chit and Eugene was recorded for Ultraphone. We recorded again the 31st of January '36 for His Master's Voice and did "I'm in the Mood for Love" and "After You've Gone". Those two records added more to my European success than the Fats Waller ones in the sense that I had more solo space and I was…

A little earlier than the January 31st date with Chittison and d'Hellemes, I recorded "Coquette" and the first number I ever composed called "Joe Louis Stomp" with Edgar Courance (tenor), John Ferrier (piano), Oscar Aleman (guitar), Eugene d'Hellemes (bass), and William Diemar (drums). This date is registered in the French discography as being done on the 31st of January also but I don't remember having two recording dates the same day.

A few months after New Year's day 1936, it must have been in February, Freddy didn't come to work one night. Spider, George Johnson, were paid the equivalent of fifty dollars a week which was very good salary for a musician working in France as living expenses were about half of what they were in the U.S.A. The custom in France was and still is that musicians and other artists working in night clubs are paid every night.
